# W0 synthetic contract fixtures

These small JSON documents and manually written expectations freeze the C03-C08
representative oracle before implementation. They use reserved `.invalid`
addresses, contain no provider source or production evidence, and make no claim
about a provider's actual wire protocol, current production inventory, UI,
execution support, deployment, or publication readiness. Do not call the servers
or fetch the negative external reference.

No fixture or expected graph is generated by the runtime projector, Docs composer,
website loader, MCP compiler, Router compiler, or their helpers. The expectations
are concrete examples of the spec's semantics, not a replacement schema language
or a second composer. The expected effective graph is an oracle representation;
W1 adapters may map an existing consumer view to it without changing execution.

## Files and case mapping

| Fixture / case | Criteria | Required observation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 3.1 `parameters-and-public-inheritance` | C03 | Path/query/header/cookie; `(in,name)` override; parameter `content`; style/explode/allowReserved; public root/path/operation servers; inherited and cleared security |
| 3.1 `request-media-encoding-and-examples` | C03, C07, C08 | Required body; every declared media; form/multipart encoding and part headers; literal `$ref` data; explicit null |
| 3.1 `schema-shapes-and-constraints` | C04 | Nested object/map, array, scalar, null, true/false/empty schemas; bounds, enum/const/default, composition, conditionals and dependencies |
| 3.1 `finite-recursive-shared-escaped-closure` | C05 | Recursive closure terminates; shared targets are one declaration; RFC 6901 `~1` and `~0` resolve; instance `$ref` stays data |
| 3.1 `all-statuses-public-headers-links-and-body-states` | C06, C07 | 200/201/204/205/2XX/400/default; public headers/links; unknown vs unconstrained vs no-content; JSON/+json/text/binary/SSE/NDJSON |
| 3.1 `example-location-null-absence-invalid-and-literal-ref` | C05, C08 | Media/named/referenced/schema examples remain at their declared locations; null is present; absent stays absent; invalid example is retained and flagged |
| 3.1 `declared-callback-and-webhook` | C05, C06 | Callback runtime expression and webhook operation remain retrievable, with referenced schema closure; unsupported consumer rendering reports a named limitation |
| 3.1 `reserved-property-and-response-names-are-declarations` | C04-C06 | Schema properties named value/example/default/enum/const and a response named default still contain real references; keyword/data exclusions must respect context |
| 3.1 `literal-dollar-ref-property-name` | C04, C05, C08 | A property literally named `$ref` is a schema-map entry; its declared property schema is a real reference, while its example is instance data |
| 3.0 `oas30-source-semantics` and six conversion oracles | C04-C06, C08 | Raw declaration stays available; nullable and Boolean exclusive bounds convert with equivalent validation; enum is not widened |
| `broken-local-ref` | C05 | Missing local schema is a named failure, not `{}` or a dropped response |
| `unknown-external-ref` | C05 | Unavailable external reference is a named limitation/failure; offline check cannot silently fetch or fake a schema |

The effective GET graph includes full response declarations, public inherited
servers/security, parameters after reference resolution and override, and the
reachable component declarations needed by those preserved references. Parameter
array order is a fixture convention: retain path positions, replace an overridden
`(in,name)` at that position, and append new operation parameters. An adapter may
compare parameters by `(in,name)` rather than require a product's display order.
The graph resolves the parameter reference to make the override rule observable;
it retains schema/example references and their finite reachable declarations.
The escaped target is a `$defs` member of `EscapedDefinitions`; names containing
`/` or `~` are legal there without violating OpenAPI component-name restrictions.
The literal `$ref` name is a property name, not an OpenAPI component name.

Five additional fixed lossless declaration graphs require consumer adapters to
compare every declared schema, the complete POST body (all six media and encoding),
POST text/SSE/binary/false-schema responses, nullable GET named/null/literal
examples, and the list GET NDJSON response. These are literal JSON expectations
reviewed from the independently authored synthetic declarations and stored in the
manifest before any target conversion. They do not reuse a consumer's output.

## Manifest format

Each `*.expected.json` has `format_version: 1`, `fixture`, and `cases`.
Each case has a stable `id`, `criteria`, `source_ref: {file,pointer}`, and raw
`assertions`. Pointers use RFC 6901, including escaped path and media names.
Each assertion has exactly one of:

- `equals`: JSON structural equality, including explicit null/false/empty values.
- `subset`: recursively present expected object keys; arrays/scalars compare
  exactly. This is available for adapters; the initial raw assertions use equality.
- `absent: true`: the pointer must not exist; null does not count as absent.

`cases[].schema_examples` contains `{schema_pointer,instance,valid}`. It validates
instances against the referenced 3.1 schema with a standard independent JSON
Schema 2020-12 validator and this fixed document as the local reference resource.
Do not recursively interpret `$ref` keys in instances, `example`, Example Object
`value`, schema `examples`, enum/default/const values, or link expression strings
as schema references. In contrast, Example Object `$ref` and Schema Object `$ref`
are references. Invalid examples are deliberately included; they must remain
declared examples even though validation reports that they do not satisfy schema.

`consumer_expectations` is a list of `{id,kind,criteria,source_ref,expected}`:

- `effective_operation`, `effective_servers`, `effective_security`: independently
  authored effective public context and operation graph.
- `lossless_declaration`: the complete declaration at the exact `source_ref`
  pointer, with all original schemas, media, encoding, examples, and references.
  This graph preserves raw declarations; effective inheritance/override uses the
  separate effective-context oracles. Reference resolution must not flatten or
  coerce the raw declaration graph.
- `reference_closure`: a sorted set of reachable reference URI strings. Include
  a recursive back-edge target once; do not inline forever or include instance
  values. The starting declaration is not itself counted unless an actual
  reachable reference targets it.
- `response_definition_states`: explicit states for unknown, unconstrained, and
  no-content declarations; these are documentation states, not admission policy.
- `callback_webhook_declarations`: the callback mapping, its referenced public
  callback declaration, and full declared webhook operations. A consumer that
  cannot render them must still preserve a same-version retrievable declaration
  and name its display limitation; no callback execution is added.
- `oas30_conversion`: a fixed expected JSON Schema 2020-12 schema. Optional
  `schema_examples` validates instances against this **expected** schema. This
  checks oracle consistency, not whether an actual converter produced it.

For 3.0, nullable adds null only when type is explicitly declared in that Schema
Object. Other constraints remain in force: `enum: ["ok"]` still rejects null.
`exclusiveMinimum: true` with `minimum: 0` becomes numeric `exclusiveMinimum: 0`;
false keeps the inclusive bound. Do not treat numeric zero as a missing bound.
The 3.0 raw schema is not a JSON Schema 2020-12 input; validate the expected
conversion instead of letting a validator silently ignore nullable.

`negative_expectations` contains `{id,kind,criteria,source_ref,ref,reason,expected,must_not}`.
It specifies required failure semantics for future consumer adapters. Raw
verification checks that the failure precondition exists; it must not claim that
the target implementation rejected it until an adapter actually exercises that
implementation. `source_ref` always identifies the exact declaration to compare
or the reference location to report; file names are relative to this directory.

## Preservation versus conversion

The raw assertion cases require lossless preservation. Media, examples, headers,
links, true/false schemas, missing schema, and literal instance values must not
be coerced into a JSON-object-only view. The 3.1 consumer oracles additionally
require inheritance/override and finite reference closure. Only the 3.0 conversion
oracles require dialect conversion; equivalent schema semantics may be compared
via the fixed expected schemas and instances rather than arbitrary textual order.

Fixture checks can establish that these inputs and expectations are internally
consistent. W1 must still compare each real consumer and its actual detail/UI
entry points. C08 cURL rendering must also be checked through the existing request
compiler in that phase; this fixture does not invent a parallel cURL compiler.
No test here establishes C01/C02 full-inventory onboarding, source freshness,
formal debt approval, required CI status, publication activation, or live
convergence. Those need the separate W0 inputs and later implementation evidence.

The parent acceptance package documents the offline validation command. This
directory intentionally contains data and explanations only, with no execution
adapter, network probe, or business-code dependency.
